title: How a hash map finds a key
alt: Two different keys can land in the same bucket. The map then checks each one in that bucket, which is still faster than reading the whole list.

caption.text: A hash map keeps a row of numbered buckets.

bubbles.text: To store a key, I turn it into a number first.
Like a fingerprint for the word?
Yes. "Cat" always comes out as 2, so cat goes in bucket 2.
So I get the same number and look in one bucket?
One look instead of a search. That is the whole trick!
